sheet-83-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 83 shows the northwestern end of Caldwell along Bloomfield Avenue, from Prospect Avenue at the bottom of the sheet north past Lane Avenue towards the West Caldwell fork shown on sheet 91. It is drawn at 60 feet to an inch, larger than the 100-foot sheets of the town centre, with north towards the right of the page, so Bloomfield Avenue runs diagonally down the sheet. The largest property is the Lane & Lockward Co. tobacco factory on the west side of Bloomfield Avenue north of Lane Avenue: a frame works with rooms for shipping, cutting, packing, storage, printing and a dry room, an engine room and chimney, a shed and storage building, a coal house and a separate tobacco warehouse, with a note that there is no watchman, heat is from stoves, power from steam and lights from oil. South of the factory, Lane Avenue runs west from Bloomfield Avenue between long narrow house lots, most with a single frame dwelling and small outbuildings. East of Bloomfield Avenue scattered frame dwellings, store houses and hen houses stand on large lots. At the bottom edge Prospect Avenue crosses the sheet, with Academy Road leaving it to the south toward sheet 84. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and a hydrant are marked on Bloomfield Avenue and Prospect Avenue; Bloomfield Avenue is shown 66 feet wide. A boxed inset in the lower left of the sheet, part 2, continues Lane Avenue to the west.
notes: Prospect Avenue is today Prospect Street.
Lane & Lockward Co. tobacco factory on Bloomfield Avenue north of Lane Avenue.
Placed from three junctions only (an exact fit); low confidence away from Bloomfield Avenue.

Caldwell / West Caldwell line, 60 ft. Bloomfield Av, Lane Av, Prospect Av (now Prospect Street), Academy Road at bottom. Lane & Lockward Co tobacco factory. Part 1 main; part 2 boxed inset continuing Lane Av west of part 1 (same double dwelling drawn on both; placed by carried points).

sheet-83-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 83 is a boxed inset in the lower left of the sheet that continues Lane Avenue westward from the point where part 1 is cut by the sheet edge; the printed number 83 at both cut ends marks the join. It is drawn at the same scale, 60 feet to an inch, and with the same orientation as part 1, with its own small north arrow pointing towards the right of the page. The inset shows a single strip of Lane Avenue, 35 feet wide, with house lots lettered A to E along its south side and further lots to the north. The lots are deep and narrow and mostly built with one frame dwelling each, several of them two storeys, with small sheds, a hen house and other outbuildings behind; the double dwelling at the east end of the inset is the same building drawn at the west end of part 1. Much of the inset is open ground marked with block numbers only. No cross street, water pipe or hydrant is shown in the inset. It belongs to the scattered residential edge of Caldwell towards the West Caldwell line.
notes: Placed by carrying two points from the double dwelling drawn on both parts of the sheet, at the scale and rotation of part 1; low confidence.

Caldwell / West Caldwell line, 60 ft. Bloomfield Av, Lane Av, Prospect Av (now Prospect Street), Academy Road at bottom. Lane & Lockward Co tobacco factory. Part 1 main; part 2 boxed inset continuing Lane Av west of part 1 (same double dwelling drawn on both; placed by carried points).

sheet-84.description: Sheet 84 covers the northern edge of Caldwell, where Prospect Avenue runs along the top of the sheet and Academy Road and Bloomfield Avenue run down the page and converge towards the bottom. It is drawn at 60 feet to an inch, a larger scale than the 100 foot town sheets, with north towards the right, so the streets run diagonally across the page. The main feature is the Monomonock Inn, a large seasonal hotel set back between Academy Road and Bloomfield Avenue, drawn in yellow frame with a pink brick wing at its east end; its notes say it is open from May to November, lit by electricity, heated by steam, and protected by hose, extinguishers, a watchman and an electric clock, with a dining hall, cottage, store room, laundry and kitchen shown on the plan. West of Academy Road stands the Caldwell Public School, a pink brick building with steam heat and electric lights. The rest of the sheet is thinly built: a few dwellings along Thomas and Elizabeth on the west side of Academy Road, with long narrow lots marked out but mostly empty, and a handful of dwellings beside Bloomfield Avenue. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches and hydrants are drawn along the main roads, and street widths of 50, 60 and 66 feet are printed. Campbell Avenue branches off Bloomfield Avenue at the foot of the sheet. The sheet carries the Caldwell Borough heading and block numbers 1 to 4, and joins sheet 83 above and sheet 85 below.
notes: Prospect Avenue is today Prospect Street.
Thomas and Elizabeth are printed without a suffix; today Thomas Street and Elizabeth Street.
Campbell Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap; it may be today's Central Avenue, but a trial including that junction fitted badly (leave-one-out 8 m), so it was not used.
Drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north towards the right; fitted rotation about 49 degrees.
Placed from four junctions, three of them along Academy Road: low to medium confidence in rotation.
Caldwell, 60 ft. Prospect Av (now Prospect Street), Academy Road, Thomas, Elizabeth, Bloomfield Av, Campbell Av. Caldwell Public School, Monomonock Inn. One part.

sheet-85.description: Sheet 85 covers the southwest part of Caldwell, between Bloomfield Avenue along the top and Westville Avenue, which crosses the sheet as a long diagonal from the lower left to the upper right. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The left half is a compact residential district laid out in long narrow lots between Elizabeth, Washburn Place and Gould Place, mostly built with frame dwellings and many lots still vacant; Caldwell Methodist Episcopal Church (heated by furnace, lit by electricity) stands near Cleveland Street, and a hall of the C.B.I.A. with a bowling alley and a wood-sawing shop are drawn among the dwellings. Along the top edge, Bloomfield Avenue carries a short row of shops and houses, including a bakery, an ice cream factory with its gas engine, a garage and cement block works, and the Masonic lodge. A brook drawn in blue enters from the top near Brookside Avenue and runs south through a small pond, where a second branch joins it from the northeast; the pond and brook divide the built-up part from the open ground below. At the upper right the First Presbyterian Church stands on Bloomfield Avenue near the Westville Avenue junction. At the right edge, beside the line of the former railroad, are S. J. Speer's coal yard and Gosman Brothers' feed and hay store, with a few dwellings along Roseland. The whole southern half of the sheet is open land with only scattered buildings. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches and hydrants follow the main streets, and street widths of 40, 50, 58, 60 and 75 feet are printed. A compass rose and the 100 foot scale bar are at the lower left.
notes: Elizabeth is printed without a suffix; today Elizabeth Street.
Campbell Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap; it is drawn at the upper left edge and also on sheets 84 and 87.
Brookside Avenue was left out of the fit: its junction with Westville Avenue sat 12 m from the fit, so the modern street may not follow the 1907 line.
Drawn with north to the upper left; fitted rotation about -36 degrees.
The Erie Railroad Caldwell Branch (abandoned) is drawn at the lower right.
Caldwell, 100 ft. Bloomfield Av, Elizabeth, Washburn Pl, Gould Pl, Westville Av, Brookside Av, Roseland Av, Academy Road. First Presbyterian Church. Erie RR Caldwell Branch at lower right. One part.

sheet-86-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 86 covers the area south of Bloomfield Avenue between Roseland Avenue and Arlington Avenue in Caldwell, reaching south to the Essex Fells borough line. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Along Bloomfield Avenue stand the Caldwell fire house, home of one hose company and a hook and ladder truck with a bell tower, a few frame dwellings and St. Aloysius R.C. Church. A brook drawn in blue runs from the fire house east behind the Bloomfield Avenue frontage through a pond. The Erie Railroad Caldwell Branch crosses the sheet in a long curve from the southwest, crossing Roseland Avenue and running northeast to the Caldwell passenger station and freight station near Arlington Avenue, beside a second pond and a wind wheel tower. Roseland Avenue is lined on its east side by a row of frame dwellings near Bloomfield Avenue and, further south, by a few houses, a saloon and Wilson's Hotel at the Essex Fells line. The large central block is open ground with the convent of the Sisters of St. Dominic, a brick building with electric light and steam heat, and a water tank tower. Oak Grove Road is drawn as a dashed, unbuilt road east of Roseland Avenue. The lower right of the sheet is a separate inset of the Kingsley School at 50 feet to an inch (part 2).
notes: Oak Grove Road is drawn as a proposed (dashed) road.
The Erie Railroad Caldwell Branch is abandoned; its crossing of Roseland Avenue was used as a hand-picked control point from the former line in OpenStreetMap.
Sisters of St. Dominic convent in the central block.

Caldwell, 100 ft. Roseland Av, Bloomfield Av, Westville Av, Forest Av, Arlington Av, Oak Grove Road (dashed, proposed), Erie RR Caldwell Branch (abandoned) and Caldwell passenger station, St Aloysius RC Church, Sisters of St Dominic convent. Part 1 main; part 2 boxed inset of the Kingsley School campus at 50 ft (Essex Fells), not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Kingsley School campus, Essex Fells, 50 ft to an inch (Oak Lane dashed, Erie RR Caldwell Branch at its edge) (no street junction; Oak Lane drawn as a proposed road and its position against today's Oak Lane and the former railway could not be settled; needs identification of the campus site; then parcel corners or the former railway line (step 6b)).

sheet-87.description: Sheet 87 covers the centre of Caldwell north of Bloomfield Avenue, from Campbell Avenue on the west to Smull Avenue on the east. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left, so the grid of streets runs diagonally across the page, and a compass rose stands in the empty ground at the top. Bloomfield Avenue, 75 feet wide, is the commercial frontage along the foot of the sheet, with a hardware store, a plumber, a garage, a barber shop and post office in a brick building, the Caldwell House with its saloon, pool room and bowling alley, and Husks Livery. North of it the sheet is a planned residential district of frame dwellings in long narrow lots on Cleveland, Hanford Place and Whitfield, with many lots empty; a foundation, a carpenter's shop and a building marked Italian Quarters are among the buildings. Central Avenue runs as a diagonal across the upper left and then turns south, bounding the built-up blocks; Park Avenue and Myrtle Avenue serve a second block of lots at the upper right, where a Y-shaped pond and a narrow stream are drawn in blue. Campbell Avenue runs along the left edge, with dwellings and a lumber house on its east side. The open ground in the middle of the sheet, numbered block 3, is mostly vacant. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches with hydrants follow the main streets, and street widths of 50 and 75 feet are printed. Block numbers 1 to 7 are printed in the blocks. The sheet joins sheet 84 to the west and sheet 85 below, and the margin carries the Caldwell and W. Caldwell Borough heading.
notes: Whitfield and Cleveland are printed without a suffix; today Whitfield Street and Cleveland Street.

Campbell Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap; its line probably survives as part of modern Central Avenue, whose junctions with Whitfield and Bloomfield Avenue fitted 4 to 5 m worse than the other streets, so they were not used.
The Central Avenue drawn here (a diagonal turning south beside Park Avenue) is not the same line as today's Central Avenue.
Brookside Avenue was left out of the fit: its junction with Bloomfield Avenue was not detected.
Drawn with north to the upper left; fitted rotation about -45 degrees.
Caldwell, 100 ft. Bloomfield Av, Campbell Av, Central Av, Whitfield, Cleveland, Hanford Pl, Park Av, Myrtle Av, Smull Av, Brookside Av. One part.

sheet-88.description: Sheet 88 covers the eastern part of Caldwell's business and residential centre on the north side of Bloomfield Avenue, from Smull Avenue on the west to Arlington Avenue on the east, and north to Hatfield and Myrtle Avenue. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left, so the streets run diagonally to true north. Along Bloomfield Avenue, at Personette, stands a short row of one- and two-storey shops: a furniture store, offices, a plumber, a bank and drug store shown in brick, a tin shop and stores, with a post office and further stores east of it. Behind the frontage the sheet is residential: frame dwellings on Personette, Kirkwood Place, Forest Avenue, Crane, Hillside Avenue, Hatfield and Arlington Avenue, laid out in long narrow lots with many still empty. A Baptist church stands at Bloomfield Avenue and Forest Avenue, and the house near the east end of the Bloomfield Avenue frontage is marked as the birthplace of former President Grover Cleveland. At the west edge, on Smull Avenue, is the Grover House, a seasonal hotel open from May to October lit by electricity and gas, with its annex and a servants' building. A brook drawn in blue runs from the north edge south between Smull Avenue and Forest Avenue, joined by a straight ditch, and two unnamed dashed roads cross the open ground west of it. Lumber sheds stand west of Forest Avenue. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches with hydrants are marked along the main streets. Block numbers 1 to 7 are printed in the blocks.
notes: Birthplace of President Grover Cleveland marked on Bloomfield Avenue (the Old First Church manse, now the Grover Cleveland Birthplace historic site).
Hatfield and Crane are printed without a suffix; today Hatfield Street and Crane Street.
Personette is printed without a suffix; today Personette Street.
Drawn with north to the upper left; fitted rotation about -46 degrees.
Caldwell, 100 ft. Bloomfield Av, Smull Av, Personette, Kirkwood Pl, Forest Av, Crane, Hillside Av, Hatfield, Arlington Av, Myrtle Av. Grover House, Cleveland birthplace. One part. Pilot sheet.

sheet-89.description: Sheet 89 covers the southeast part of Caldwell, along Bloomfield Avenue where the Erie Railroad's Caldwell Branch runs beside the street, and extends south to the line of Essex Fells Borough. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the top. Across the upper left Arlington Avenue runs diagonally from the lower left to the upper right and is crossed by Crane and Hatfield, each 60 feet wide, with a few frame dwellings along them. Hatfield runs east to Mountain Avenue at the right edge, where Little Place leaves it. Wide empty blocks in the middle of the sheet are crossed by two dashed roads marked as having no name, which are proposed streets. Bloomfield Avenue, 75 feet wide, crosses the sheet from left to right, with the Caldwell Branch tracks and the Caldwell passenger station at the left, a locomotive house, and the yards of Slayback Brothers, lumber and coal, and James A. Speer and Son, flour, feed and hay, with lumber sheds, a coal house and store houses around the sidings. Old Grove Road, drawn in dashed lines as a proposed road, leaves the railroad yard to the south. Ryerson Avenue, 66 feet wide, runs south from Bloomfield Avenue toward the bottom of the sheet. In the lower right the Oak Hill Sanitarium stands in open grounds, with a main building, an east cottage and a south cottage, west of the dash and dot line of the Essex Fells Borough boundary. Water mains and hydrants are marked along the main streets, block numbers 1 to 6 are printed, and the 100 foot scale bar is at the lower left.
notes: Crane and Hatfield are printed without a suffix; today Crane Street and Hatfield Street.
Old Grove Road is drawn dashed and is not in OpenStreetMap; it was not used.
The Erie Railroad Caldwell Branch drawn along Bloomfield Avenue is abandoned; it is not in the running-line data, so no rail control was used.
Drawn with north to the top; fitted rotation about -8 degrees.
The diagonal Mountain Av (from Crane to the east edge) is today Elm Road; the vertical Mountain Av at the east edge is today's Mountain Avenue.
The two dashed roads marked (No Name) are today Erwin Place (west) and Linwood Terrace (east).

Placed from Arlington Avenue at Hatfield and Crane, Crane Street / Elm Road and a hand-picked Bloomfield Avenue / Ryerson Avenue; Arlington / Bloomfield (a curved junction) and the junctions on modern Mountain Avenue (15 to 25 m off) were left out. Low confidence.

Caldwell / Essex Fells, 100 ft, north up. Arlington Av, Crane, Hatfield, Mountain Av (diagonal = Elm Road; east-edge Mountain Av = Mountain Avenue, drawn 15-25 m from today's line), Bloomfield Av, Ryerson Av, Old Grove Road (dashed), two (No Name) dashed roads (Erwin Place, Linwood Terrace), Erie RR station and yards, Oak Hill Sanitarium. One part.

sheet-90.description: Sheet 90 covers the northeast edge of Caldwell, where the borough meets North Caldwell, Essex Fells and Verona Township. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the top. Most of the sheet is open land. Mountain Avenue, 50 feet wide, runs down the left side from the top to Old Road, with scattered frame dwellings along it, and is met by Hatfield Street from the west and Little Place from the east; a dashed road leaves it near the top and a few outbuildings stand beside it. A dash and dot line running down the middle of the sheet is the boundary between Caldwell Borough and North Caldwell Borough, and another near the right edge divides North Caldwell from Verona Township. The principal feature is the Essex County Penitentiary at the centre right: a cross-shaped cell block of North, West and East wings drawn in blue, with a hospital and laundry, boiler and store rooms, a general store house, a tower, hen houses and other farm buildings beside it, ringed by 4 inch water pipes and hydrants with 100 and 200 feet of hose. Its note records steam heat, electric and gas light, coal fuel and a Worthington pump. A pond lies south east of the buildings. In the lower part of the sheet Old Road crosses from the left and Bloomfield Avenue runs along the bottom with the railroad corridor, with a few dwellings along both. The sheet carries the heading for Caldwell and North Caldwell Borough, block numbers 1 to 4 and the 100 foot scale bar at the bottom.
notes: The Erie Railroad Caldwell Branch (abandoned) is drawn along Bloomfield Avenue at the bottom.
Drawn with north to the top.

Placed by two points carried from sheet 89 (Hatfield Street / Mountain Avenue and the Mountain Avenue / Old Road junction as drawn on both sheets); today's Mountain Avenue lies 15 to 25 m from where these sheets draw it, so the modern junction coordinates were not used. Low confidence.
The Mountain Av running west from the Old Road junction is today Elm Road; Little Place and Old Road were not identified with confidence.

Caldwell / North Caldwell / Essex Fells, 100 ft, north up. Bloomfield Av, Mountain Av, Little Pl, Hatfield St, Old Road; Essex County Penitentiary. One part, placed by two points carried from sheet 89.

sheet-91-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 91 follows Bloomfield Avenue north through West Caldwell to the fork where Old Road branches north and Dutch Lane branches east, with Bloomfield Avenue continuing northwest toward Pine Brook. It is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right, so Bloomfield Avenue runs straight up the page. The frontage is a loose string of frame dwellings, a store and dwelling with a vacant shop shown in brick, a pool room, a blacksmith shop and outbuildings. A brook crosses Bloomfield Avenue under a short bridge in the lower half of the sheet. On the west side two narrow lanes, each lettered only Lane and drawn 20 and 15 feet wide, lead off Bloomfield Avenue; on the first stands the H. F. Backus milk depot with its ice house and boiler. At the fork are a store, the Union Chapel and, on Dutch Lane, the C. A. Harrison milk depot with an ice house, dwellings and barns. Much of the sheet beyond the frontages is open ground. The right half of the sheet holds two boxed insets of other places: Old Road at Passaic Avenue with the Francisco dairy farm (part 2) and Bloomfield Avenue at Pine Brook (part 3).
notes: Old Road is today Clinton Road; Dutch Lane is today Fairfield Avenue.
The first lane west of Bloomfield Avenue is taken to be today's Melrose Place; the second has no modern counterpart.
Two-point helmert fit (the fork and Melrose Place); low confidence.

West Caldwell / Caldwell Township, 60 ft. Part 1: Bloomfield Av to the fork with Old Road (now Clinton Road) and Dutch Lane (now Fairfield Avenue), two lanes on the west side (first = Melrose Place). Part 2: boxed inset of Old Road at Passaic Av with the Francisco dairy farm. Part 3: boxed inset at Pine Brook (Bloomfield Av, Old Road, Pine Brook Hotel), not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Bloomfield Avenue at Pine Brook, Pine Brook Hotel, Old Road (no identifiable junction: Old Road is drawn dashed and the old Bloomfield Avenue alignment at Pine Brook is cut by US 46; needs identification of Old Road at Pine Brook; parcel corners (step 6b)).

sheet-91-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 91 is a boxed inset in the lower right of the sheet showing Old Road where Passaic Avenue meets it from the west, north of the West Caldwell fork shown in part 1. It is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with its own north arrow. Old Road is drawn 35 to 40 feet wide running up the length of the inset and bending slightly at its upper end; Passaic Avenue is a short stub at the left edge. East of Old Road lies the W. H. & R. S. Francisco dairy farm, noted as averaging 90 head of cattle: a long two-storey barn, a large L-shaped barn, a wagon shed, a milk bottling house, a store house, an ice house, a wagon house, a hen house and a dwelling with a wash house drawn in brick, and at the far right a two-and-a-half-storey barn with an incline and a portable boiler and engine. Two further dwellings face Old Road. The rest of the inset is open land with no lot lines.
notes: Old Road is today Clinton Road.
W. H. & R. S. Francisco dairy farm, about 90 head of cattle.
Placed from one hand-picked junction (Clinton Road / Passaic Avenue) at the scale and rotation of part 1; low confidence.

West Caldwell / Caldwell Township, 60 ft. Part 1: Bloomfield Av to the fork with Old Road (now Clinton Road) and Dutch Lane (now Fairfield Avenue), two lanes on the west side (first = Melrose Place). Part 2: boxed inset of Old Road at Passaic Av with the Francisco dairy farm. Part 3: boxed inset at Pine Brook (Bloomfield Av, Old Road, Pine Brook Hotel), not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Bloomfield Avenue at Pine Brook, Pine Brook Hotel, Old Road (no identifiable junction: Old Road is drawn dashed and the old Bloomfield Avenue alignment at Pine Brook is cut by US 46; needs identification of Old Road at Pine Brook; parcel corners (step 6b)).

sheet-92-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 92 covers the right half of the sheet in West Caldwell, around the junction where Lane Avenue comes in from the north, Westville Avenue runs east toward Caldwell and Brookside Avenue leaves to the south. It is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. At the top right is the Cloverdale Dairy Farm, noted at 40 head of cattle, with a bottling house, a dwelling and a large two-storey barn. Along the west side of Brookside Avenue just south of the junction stands A. Russell's general repair shop: a store house, a blacksmith shop with storage above, wood working and a paint shop. East of Brookside Avenue are the J. M. Jacobus cigar factory, a two-storey frame building, a few dwellings, a hen house and, further south, the Fairview Dairy Farm of 90 head of cattle with an ice machine and bottling house, an ice house, wagon and store houses and long barns with a fodder chopper and a portable engine. Most of the part is open land divided into large lots. Westville Avenue is drawn 60 feet wide and Lane and Brookside Avenues 35 feet. The left half of the sheet belongs to other parts drawn at other orientations.
notes: Brookside Avenue here is today Runnymede Road; it is not the Brookside Avenue of Caldwell.
Cloverdale and Fairview dairy farms; J. M. Jacobus cigar factory.
Placed from one hand-picked junction (Lane Avenue / Westville Avenue) at the atlas scale with rotation from the sheet's compass and the modern streets; low confidence.

West Caldwell (old Clinton) and Caldwell Township, 60 ft. Part 1: Lane Av / Westville Av / Brookside Av (now Runnymede Road) junction, Cloverdale and Fairview dairy farms. Part 2: Passaic Av / Westville Av, M S Crane mill and Mill Pond, Meadow Lane (own north arrow). Part 3: boxed inset of Clinton Av and Pine Brook Road with the Clinton M E Church, not placed. Part 4: boxed inset of the Clinton Public School on Clinton Av and Fairfield Road, not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Clinton Avenue and Pine Brook Road, Clinton M. E. Church (1907 Clinton Av and Pine Brook Road could not be matched to modern streets (north arrow straight up, Pine Brook Road running northeast on the page); needs identification of the Clinton M. E. Church site).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Clinton Public School, Clinton Avenue and Fairfield Road (1907 Clinton Av / Fairfield Road junction could not be matched to modern streets; needs identification of the junction).

sheet-92-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 92 covers the left side of the sheet around the junction of Passaic Avenue and Westville Avenue in West Caldwell, with its own north arrow pointing to the upper right. It is drawn at 60 feet to an inch. The upper half is taken up by the M. S. Crane saw, planing and feed mill on the stream that feeds the Mill Pond: lumber sheds, a wagon house with a hay loft, a repair shop, a corn house, an ice house, hen, wood and store houses, a cement chimney and the mill buildings for sawing, planing and feed, with notes on its water and steam power, machinery and oil lighting. A log yard lies beside the Mill Pond, whose outlet passes under Passaic Avenue at a small bridge and flows south into a larger pond. Meadow Lane runs along the left edge of the sheet. Passaic Avenue is drawn 50 feet wide crossing the sheet; Westville Avenue, 60 feet wide, runs south from it past the farm buildings of Caleb Crane, a group of barns, a dwelling and an ice house. Much of the rest is open land. Insets of the Clinton district (parts 3 and 4) are boxed off at the top and lower left.
notes: M. S. Crane saw, planing and feed mill and the farm buildings of Caleb Crane.
Meadow Lane has no modern counterpart in the reference data.
